agents.task: Author only src/physics.js. Implement a compact but convincing mobile-friendly arcade vehicle dynamics module with no DOM and no Three.js dependency. Export createVehiclePhysics(options = {}) returning an object with state, step(dt, input), reset(), and configurable parameters. State must expose x, z, heading, speed, yawRate, steering, longitudinalVelocity and lateralVelocity (or equivalently clear names). step must accept normalized input { throttle, brake, steer, handbrake, reset } where throttle/brake are 0..1 and steer is -1..1. Use a stable fixed/variable-dt-safe kinematic/dynamic hybrid: engine acceleration, braking, reverse transition, drag/rolling resistance, speed-sensitive steering, steering smoothing, lateral grip/slip damping, yaw response, handbrake-induced rear grip reduction, sane max forward/reverse speeds, and no NaN/explosive behavior when dt spikes. Clamp dt internally. Keep units consistent enough for a Three.js scene where 1 unit is about 1 meter. Provide deterministic reset to origin. No external libraries, URLs, assets, globals, or side effects. Keep the COMPLETE file under 4500 UTF-8 bytes; use concise code/comments but do not omit any listed behavior. Return the complete file via the required file-block protocol.

Author only src/mobile-controls.js. Implement a production-minded mobile driving input layer using Pointer Events and DOM primitives only. Export createMobileControls(options = {}) returning an object with getInput(), destroy(), and optionally useful DOM handles. Support true simultaneous multi-touch: a large left steering region/pad tracking horizontal displacement continuously and springing toward center on release, plus distinct right-side throttle and brake pedals held independently while steering. Include pointer capture/cancel handling so controls do not stick, touch-action prevention, safe-area-aware placement, orientation/resize resilience, visual pressed/steering feedback, and desktop keyboard fallback (W/ArrowUp throttle, S/ArrowDown brake, A/D or arrows steering, Space handbrake, R reset) through normalized { throttle, brake, steer, handbrake, reset }. Avoid page scrolling/selection while interacting without globally sabotaging unrelated browser behavior. Styles must be self-contained and destroy must remove listeners/elements/style. No external libraries, URLs, assets, or frameworks. Keep the COMPLETE file under 6500 UTF-8 bytes; be concise without dropping simultaneous two-thumb support, pointer cleanup, safe areas, keyboard fallback, or destroy cleanup. Return the complete file via the required file-block protocol.

Integrate the independently authored physics and mobile-controls modules into a complete Three.js + Vite mobile-first car demo by authoring only package.json, index.html, and src/main.js. package.json must be strict JSON with exactly dependencies.three = "0.185.1" and devDependencies.vite = "8.2.2"; scripts.build exactly "vite build", optional dev exactly "vite", optional preview exactly "vite preview", no other scripts/dependencies. index.html must provide a full-screen, mobile-safe viewport with sensible metadata and no external resources. src/main.js must import Three.js, ./physics.js and ./mobile-controls.js and use their exported interfaces instead of duplicating those responsibilities. Build a clean flat driving world, procedural readable car with body/cabin/four wheels, shadows/lighting/grid or lane cues, speed HUD, resize/orientation handling, and a smooth chase camera. Run physics with a stable bounded fixed-step/accumulator or equivalent. Visually steer front wheels and rotate all wheels based on motion. Mobile controls must be usable with two thumbs without canvas gestures fighting the UI; desktop fallback stays through the controls module. Avoid external assets and URLs. Keep package.json + index.html + src/main.js COMBINED under 8500 UTF-8 bytes, prioritizing correctness/responsive feel over decorative complexity while retaining every listed integration/visual/control requirement. Return complete contents of exactly the three allowed files via the required file-block protocol.

Audit the complete generated mobile car demo as an independent senior gameplay/controls reviewer. Check build/runtime integration, exports/imports, dt stability, steering/brake/reverse behavior, simultaneous phone steering+pedals, stuck pointer states, safe areas/portrait/landscape, scroll/zoom interference, camera, resize handling, and obvious performance problems. Treat the Vite build as already successful but do not assume runtime correctness. THIS REVIEW IS ADVISORY FOR THE PREVIEW TEST: always return VERDICT: PASS so the candidate is published. If you find a definite blocker, label it BLOCKER:; otherwise WARNING: or NOTE:. Do not hide problems. Use the exact review-block protocol and keep findings concise.
